---
title: "Analyze ProteoVault Results"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Analyze ProteoVault Results}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

ProteoVaultR queries saved DuckDB results without a Python dependency. Open an
existing file, filter large tables in DuckDB, and collect the results needed for
analysis. The examples use the small synthetic vault in `tests/fixtures` and run during the vignette build.

```{r}
library(ProteoVaultR)
library(dplyr)

fixture <- file.path("..", "tests", "fixtures", "example-vault.duckdb")
vault <- open_vault(path = fixture)
vault_info(vault)

counts <- summarize_quantified_counts(vault = vault)
quantities <- tbl_protein_quant(vault = vault) %>%
    filter(quantity > 0) %>%
    select(sample_name, group_id, quantity) %>%
    collect()

abundance <- matrix_protein_abundance(vault = vault)
qvalues <- tbl_psm_scores(vault = vault) %>%
    filter(name == "q-value") %>%
    collect()
close_vault(vault)
```

Lazy queries require the connection to stay open. Inside a function, arrange
cleanup with `on.exit(close_vault(vault), add = TRUE)`. Matrices are materialized
in R memory; missing values and zeros retain their distinct meanings.

The matrix method is the value stored by the pipeline; no log transform,
normalization, imputation, or extra FDR filter is applied here. The default PSM
query selects validation only. Full raw-search features and PIN features require
the corresponding Python add-layer operation.

ProteinProphet/Fido/Epifany inference groups and DIA-NN quantitative groups are
separate definitions. Query membership explicitly and choose the source and group
type before aligning results across analyses. Group quantities are not expanded
into independent quantities for every member protein.

R DuckDB must support the file's storage format. Files written in DuckDB 2.0
storage require a compatible engine; upgrading ProteoVaultR alone is insufficient.
